decisions.reason: The bowl-removal clause is already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY, and the whisk-cleaning update requires no additional candidate-state change.
The source does not change bowl capacity or form; bowl geometry is mentioned only as a possible splash-control method.
Quick whisk detachment for cleaning does not change any food-contact material requirement.
The candidate's same-message MODIFY already records quick, simple, preferably tool-free whisk detachment.
The separate whisk-positioning clause is already captured by the candidate's same-message MODIFY; quick removal does not alter whisk-head selection or positioning state.
The source reiterates splash control through whisk position, bowl geometry, or a guard, all already represented by the candidate's current high-speed splash target and methods.
A preference for quick, preferably tool-free whisk removal does not change the prototype's off-the-shelf component strategy.
The source contains no change to input power, battery use, or electrical architecture.
The source adds a specific cleaning and swapping behavior but does not modify the general event-use reliability requirement.
Whisk removal and cleaning do not change dispensing flow, sputtering, consistency preservation, or the dispensing sequence.
The source does not change valve dripping, spout sealing, bowl sealing, or liquid-containment behavior.
Foam quality is cited as a reason to calibrate whisk height, but the candidate's required smooth and frothy result remains unchanged.
